## 1. Breakdown of the 6 Side Symbols

Flanking George Eastman’s central portrait profile are **six small square bronze panels** (three on the left, three on the right). Designed in an Art Deco, low-relief style, each symbol represents a foundational pillar of Eastman’s life, industry, and philosophy.

```
       LEFT SIDE                 RIGHT SIDE
+---------------------+   +---------------------+
| Top-Left:           |   | Top-Right:          |
| Light Rays & Prism  |   | Woven Film Web      |
+---------------------+   +---------------------+
| Middle-Left:        |   | Middle-Right:       |
| Chemical Retort     |   | Torches of Learning |
+---------------------+   +---------------------+
| Bottom-Left:        |   | Bottom-Right:       |
| Mechanical Gears    |   | Globe & Meridian    |
+---------------------+   +---------------------+

```

### Top-Left: Light Rays through a Prism (Optics & Physics)

* **Visual:** Stylized linear rays of light passing through a refraction angle / lens geometry.
* **Meaning:** Represents the physics of light and optics, the fundamental scientific basis of photography. It reflects Eastman’s obsession with capturing light accurately through precision lenses and exposure control.

### Middle-Left: Chemical Retort & Flask (Applied Chemistry)

* **Visual:** A classic glass chemical retort/flask resting over heat or set against laboratory lines.
* **Meaning:** Represents chemistry and emulsion technology. Eastman’s greatest breakthrough was transforming heavy, messy wet-plate photography into dry gelatin plates and flexible roll film through continuous chemical experimentation.

before.text: **Thomas Edison** — the man who held the invention and could not see its size. Shown Reichenbach's transparent film in 1889 he shouted to his lab, *"That's it, now work like hell!"*, then built a cabinet you look into one person at a time and defended the peep-show for years. He invented cinema's substrate and missed the scale of it. Eastman invented none of it and taxed the whole industry, engineering the 1908 MPPC so Edison's licensees could buy film only from him, with a royalty to Edison by the foot. Edison thought he was building a cartel; Eastman was building a tollbooth. In private Eastman's verdict: *"about as half baked as Henry Ford when it comes to economics."* In public: *"a phenomenal mind, a tremendous energy."* → **Kodak becomes Edison**: 1975, Sasson's filmless camera, *"that's cute, but don't tell anyone about it."* The peep-show error, sixty-seven years after Eastman wrote down what was wrong with it.

notes.chunk_at_written: … What he built in 1888 was a customer who had never existed: an ordinary person, with no chemistry and no darkroom, who could keep a piece of their own life. *You press the button, we do the rest.* It was the first true consumer company in America, and the promise was so complete that the man behind it disappeared into it. He removed himself from the product, from his gifts, from his own authorized biography, and finally from the world, on a March afternoon in 1932, with the alternative covered and a second pistol in the bookcase. The company he left ran on his instructions for eighty years without the judgment that wrote them. It gave the United States its eyes over the Soviet Union, put the first photograph of the Earth in front of humanity, and then, in a single year, 1976, invented the digital image, patented the sensor every phone now carries, licensed it out to the world, and chose to collect rent instead of build. …

notes.chunk_at_written: … What he built in 1888 was a customer who had never existed: an ordinary person, with no chemistry and no darkroom, who could keep a piece of their own life. *You press the button, we do the rest.* It was the first true consumer company in America, and the promise was so complete that the man behind it disappeared into it. He removed himself from the product, from his gifts, from his own authorized biography, and finally from the world, on a March afternoon in 1932, with the alternative covered and a second pistol in the bookcase. The company he left ran on his instructions for eighty years without the judgment that wrote them. It gave the United States its eyes over the Soviet Union, put the first photograph of the Earth in front of humanity, and then, in a single year, 1976, invented the digital image, patented the sensor every phone now carries, licensed it out to the world, and chose to collect rent instead of build. …
